prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: async_auth_flow holds context.lock for the full duration of `response = yield request`, i.e. across the entire outgoing request/response cycle, not just around the token-check/mutation. This serializes all concurrent requests on a provider behind whichever one is in flight, which is especially bad for long-running requests such as a standalone GET SSE stream that can block every other request on the same provider for its entire lifetime (tracked upstream as #2847). (3 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: All three move the request yield outside the lock so it's held only around token check/mutation. #3243 additionally replaces `lock: anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)`, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — anyio.Lock ties acquire/release to the owning task on some backends (e.g. trio), while a Semaphore does not; #2858 and #3252 leave the field typed as anyio.Lock, so they remain exposed to that cross-task release case. #2858 and #3243 both add a second lock (refresh_lock / flow_lock) so the fast proactive token-validity check on one request isn't serialized behind another request's slow in-flight reauth; #3252 keeps only the single original lock, so a concurrent request's validity check still blocks until an in-flight reauth on that same lock completes.

prs.title: Fix OAuthClientProvider._initialize() to enable transparent token refresh
prs.author: draesthetic
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider._initialize() only restores current_tokens and client_info from storage, but never recomputes token_expiry_time or restores the authorization-server metadata needed by _refresh_token(). As a result, after a process restart is_token_valid() always returns true for a stored (possibly expired) token, and even when a refresh is attempted the token endpoint can't be resolved correctly — so every restart forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (3 PRs)

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: async_auth_flow holds context.lock for the full duration of `response = yield request`, i.e. across the entire outgoing request/response cycle, not just around the token-check/mutation. This serializes all concurrent requests on a provider behind whichever one is in flight, which is especially bad for long-running requests such as a standalone GET SSE stream that can block every other request on the same provider for its entire lifetime (tracked upstream as #2847). (3 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: All three move the request yield outside the lock so it's held only around token check/mutation. #3243 additionally replaces `lock: anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)`, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — anyio.Lock ties acquire/release to the owning task on some backends (e.g. trio), while a Semaphore does not; #2858 and #3252 leave the field typed as anyio.Lock, so they remain exposed to that cross-task release case. #2858 and #3243 both add a second lock (refresh_lock / flow_lock) so the fast proactive token-validity check on one request isn't serialized behind another request's slow in-flight reauth; #3252 keeps only the single original lock, so a concurrent request's validity check still blocks until an in-flight reauth on that same lock completes.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3063 keys the in-flight check on str(request_id), which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids like int 1 and string "1" into the same key (can falsely 409 a legitimate request) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to the GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel ("_GET_stream") colliding with the standalone GET stream slot. PR #3221 introduces a type-preserving _request_stream_key() (prefixing int vs str ids, with an explicit bool-is-subclass-of-int exclusion) and documents that routing keys can never equal GET_STREAM_KEY, so it covers edge cases #3063's simpler str()-based check misses.
